solver_facing_statement: Repair the attrs behavior described by the selected public context. Public context summary: Slots class holding a reference to the original version. I have a class hierarchy implemented with slots enabled, like this: import attr ```python @attr.s(slots=True) class BaseClass(object): foo = attr.ib(default='foo') @attr.s(slots=True) class SubClass(BaseClass): bar = attr.ib(default='bar') ``` This works fine until I wanted to introspect the class hierarchy: ```python BaseClass.__subclasses__() # returns [<class '__main__.SubClass'>, <class '__main__.SubClass'>] ``` One of these is the original class, and the other is the new one created and returned by `attr.s`. This behavior manifests on both Python 3 and Python 2 (3.7.0 and 2.7.14, to be specific). Focus on the _make implementation area and preserve existing public behavior. promotion_reason: new local certification plus non-leaky public context
scope_boundaries: Modify only implementation files needed for this attrs behavior; do not edit tests or generated metadata.
solver_facing_statement: Repair the attrs behavior described by the selected public context. Public context summary: Ability to have `kw_only` attributes defined anywhere, as an optional feature. Ability to have `kw_only` attributes defined anywhere, as an optional feature (when enabled, don't raise errors if a non keyword-only attribute is defined after a keyword-only one). I'm really interested in allowing `kw_only` attrs anywhere, because it would fix the problem of not being able to add mandatory attrs to classes if the base class already has optional attrs. By making the optional attrs keyword-only, and allowing keyword-only attrs anywhere, the child classes will can add their own mandatory attrs after the otional keyword-only ones from the base class. Focus on the _make implementation area and preserve existing public behavior. Do not edit tests, generated metadata, or benchmark artifacts.
